Prostate-specific antigen monitoring
Measurement of PSA is the cornerstone of follow-up after local treatment. While PSA thresholds depend on the
local treatment used, PSA recurrence almost always precedes clinical recurrence [1436, 1437]. The key question
is to establish when a PSA rise is clinically significant since not all PSA increases have the same clinical value
(see Section 6.4.2) [994]. No prospective studies are available on the optimal timing for PSA testing and the
impact on oncological outcomes.

interventions.body:
WHAT I FOUND
**radiology_report**: The mpMRI Prostate exam identified a PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left apical peripheral zone, measuring approximately 12 x 9 x 8 mm. This lesion demonstrated restricted diffusion on DWI (b=1400) with a corresponding signal drop on the ADC map and early, focal enhancement on dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences. The impression was PI-RADS v2.1 score 4 lesion, clinical T stage cT1c, and a csPCa predicted probability of 0.8615541.
**pathology_report**: Histological examination of the prostate tissue cores revealed adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 1. The architectural growth pattern showed branching tumor tubules and not so much fusing tubules, with no cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. The tumor location was peripheral zone, apical left. The pathological trajectory across the single available biopsy timepoint remained stable at ISUP grade group 1.
**previous_notes**: On 16 Feb 2024, the patient presented with a PSA of 2.4 ng/mL. A multiparametric MRI was arranged, followed by a systematic and targeted biopsy. The biopsy confirmed ISUP grade group 1 prostate cancer. The patient was informed of the diagnosis and discussed initial management options, with a preference expressed for close monitoring rather than immediate intervention.
**family_history**: No family history was recorded.
**psa_trend**: The PSA trend shows a rise from 2.4 ng/mL in January 2024 to 3.1 ng/mL in July 2024, and further to 4.1 ng/mL in February 2025.
**laboratory_results**: The most recent PSA was 4.1 ng/mL recorded on 06 Jan 2025. Other labs included Free PSA at 0.94 ng/mL (23%), Haemoglobin at 15.1 g/dL, and eGFR >60 mL/min/1.73m2.

WHAT IS NOT RECORDED
The specific characteristics of the PI-RADS 4 lesion identified on the MRI were not explicitly detailed beyond the imaging findings. The family history was not recorded.
